answer: Coordination Harbor Pricing. Agents declare a shared "harbor": a monthly coordination quota for same-owner agents, priced as the summed pairwise overlap of their task graphs. Distinct independent agents show near-zero overlap and pay a walnut-sized base fee; cloned accounts assigned to fake independence still collide on overlap checks. Each extra identity in an overlapping harbor raises every member's fee by the full overlap score, so a sybil cluster of n pays O(n²) in ivory-tier dues.
